ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=-x+m$ intersects with $y=nx+4n\;\left(n\neq 0\right)$ at a point with an abscissa of $-2$. What is the solution set of the inequality $-x+m>nx+4n>0$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the line $y=-x+m$ intersects with $y=nx+4n (n\ne 0)$ at a point where the x-coordinate is $-2$,\\
it follows that the solution set of the inequality $-x+m>nx+4n$ with respect to $x$ is $x<-2$,\\
thus, when $y=nx+4n=0$, we have $x=-4$,\\
therefore, the solution set for the inequality $-x+m>nx+4n>0$ is $-4<x<-2$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{-4<x<-2}$.
